Every morning you get up on time is a small win. Put your feet on the floor, open the curtains and drink a glass of water. Today is a fresh start. You've got this.
Write a description, around 90 words, of a night market in a city that never sleeps.

By ten at night, the old part of the city should be asleep, but the night market is just warming up. Bright bulbs hang over rows of stalls selling kebabs, falooda, fried fish and steaming bowls of noodles. Smoke from the grills drifts over the crowd. College students share plates of chaat, while taxi drivers sip tea between rides. A man sells glowing toys that spin in the air. Music plays from somewhere. Even at midnight, the lanes are full, as if the whole city is too hungry to sleep.
We're adopting a dog from a shelter. Write a 70-word message to the family group announcing it.

Big news, everyone! On Saturday, we're bringing home a new family member: a two-year-old brown and white dog from the city animal shelter. Her name is Laddoo, and she loves belly rubs and chasing tennis balls. The shelter staff say she is gentle with children. Please come and meet her next weekend, but bring treats, because she already knows how to beg. We're so excited!
Our colleague Rekha lost her mother last week. Draft a sympathy card message from the team, about 50 words.

Dear Rekha,
We are deeply sorry for the loss of your mother. Please accept our heartfelt sympathy. We are holding you and your family in our thoughts during this difficult time. Take all the time you need, and know that we are here for you in any way that helps.
With love,
Your colleagues
Describe a beach covered in plastic after a festival, in about 80 words, for an article encouraging people to clean up.

The morning after the festival, the beach looked tired and broken. Plastic cups, torn bags and broken flower garlands lay along the shore as far as the eye could see. Bottles bobbed in the shallow waves. A dog sniffed at a pile of wrappers, and a small crab was trapped in a tangle of string. Then, slowly, people began to arrive with gloves and sacks. By noon, the sand was visible again. It showed what a few caring hands can do.
Write a short 'Student of the Month' announcement for our school newsletter, about 70 words, for Fatima Sheikh of Class 6A.

Student of the Month: Fatima Sheikh, Class 6A
This month's award goes to Fatima, who has shown kindness and hard work in equal measure. She organised a book drive that collected over 200 books for a village school, and she helps her classmates with maths during the lunch break. Her teachers say she never stops asking questions. Congratulations, Fatima! You make our whole school proud.
Write an 80-word diary entry about my first day at a swimming class as an adult. I'm 24.

Dear Diary,
At twenty-four, I finally stepped into a swimming pool for my first lesson. I was the oldest in the beginners' batch by about fifteen years. A ten-year-old girl showed me how to hold the edge and kick. I swallowed half the pool and spent most of the hour clinging to a float. But by the end, I put my face in the water without panicking. Tiny progress, but it felt huge. Same time next Tuesday!
Write a polite email, under 70 words, to my bank asking for a duplicate passbook because I lost mine.

Subject: Request for a duplicate passbook
Dear Sir or Madam,
I hold a savings account at your MG Road branch, with an account number ending in 4471. I have lost my passbook and would like to request a duplicate. Please tell me which documents I need to bring and whether any fee applies. I can visit the branch any weekday morning.
Thank you,
Lalit Arora
Help me invite all my building's neighbours to a small Ganesh Chaturthi aarti at my flat. About 60 words.

Dear neighbours,
We are bringing Ganpati Bappa home this Ganesh Chaturthi, and we would love for you to join us for the evening aarti. Please come to Flat 502 on Saturday at 7:30 pm. Prasad and modaks will be served afterwards. Children are especially welcome. Come as you are, and bring your voices for the aarti!
Warmly,
The Kulkarni family
For a teen magazine, write under 90 words about how it's okay not to be good at everything.

Nobody is good at everything, and nobody needs to be. You might be brilliant at drawing but hopeless at maths, or great at football but terrible at singing. That is completely normal. Every person has a different set of strengths. Trying new things is wonderful, even if you are bad at them, because the fun is in the learning. So be patient with yourself. Notice what you love and what you are getting better at. The rest can wait.
Describe a mango-eating session with my cousins in summer, about 80 words, for a memory journal.

Every May, my cousins and I sat on the back steps of Nani's house with a bucket of cold water full of mangoes. We didn't use knives or plates. We squeezed each mango until it was soft, bit off the top and sucked out the sweet, golden juice. It ran down our chins and elbows. The seeds were thrown into the garden, in the hope that they would grow. By the end, we were sticky from head to toe, and nobody cared at all.
In under 60 words, write the 'About Me' section for my gardening blog. I'm Joy, 23, growing vegetables on my terrace in Chennai.

Hi, I'm Joy! I'm twenty-three, and I grow vegetables in pots and old buckets on my small terrace in Chennai. What began with one chilli plant is now a jungle of tomatoes, brinjals and spinach. Here I share my successes, my many failures and everything I'm learning along the way. Grab some tea and join me!
Create a short job advertisement, about 70 words, for a part-time helper at a small bookshop.

WANTED: Part-time Bookshop Helper
Leaf and Page Bookshop is looking for a friendly, reliable helper for weekends, from 10 am to 6 pm. Duties include arranging shelves, helping customers find books and handling the billing counter. A love of reading is a must. Applicants should be at least 18 years old and comfortable with basic calculations. Interested? Visit us at 14 Lake Street with a short note about yourself.
Write a story, about 90 words, about a family whose car breaks down on a highway at night, and a kind truck driver who helps them.

Somewhere between two towns, the car coughed twice and stopped. It was nearly midnight, and the highway was dark. Mohan tried the engine again and again. Nothing. The children were frightened, and Lata held them close. Then headlights appeared, and a truck slowed down beside them. The driver, an older man with a grey beard, climbed out with a torch and a toolbox. In twenty minutes, he had found a loose wire and fixed it. He refused any money. "Just drive safely," he said, and waved them on.
Write about 50 words in very simple English describing a tiger, for my 5-year-old to read out in class.

The tiger is a big wild cat. It has orange fur with black stripes. No two tigers have the same stripes. A tiger has sharp teeth and strong legs. It can swim very well. Tigers live in forests. The tiger is the national animal of India. We must keep tigers safe.
Can you draft a note from me, a parent, to the school bus driver thanking him for always being careful with the children? About 50 words.

Dear Gurpreet ji,
Thank you for driving our children to school safely every day. My daughter tells me you always wait until each child is seated before moving, and that you greet them with a smile. Your care means a lot to all of us parents. Please accept our heartfelt thanks.
Warm regards,
Sunaina Bhalla
Describe a foggy winter evening in Delhi, in about 70 words.

By six in the evening, a thick fog has swallowed the city. Streetlights glow like blurry yellow moons, and cars crawl along with their hazard lights blinking. People hurry home with mufflers wrapped over their noses. At the corner, a group of rickshaw pullers warms their hands over a small fire. The smell of roasted peanuts and wood smoke hangs in the cold air. Sounds seem softer, as if the whole city is whispering.
My best friend and I had a fight over something silly. Write a message, about 70 words, to make up with her. Her name is Hannah.

Hi Hannah,
I've been thinking about our fight all day, and honestly, I can't even remember why it felt so important. I'm sorry for what I said. I was tired and grumpy, and I took it out on you. You're my best friend, and nothing this silly should come between us. Can we meet at our usual bench tomorrow? I'll bring the chocolate.
Love,
Saba
Write a 60-word recommendation of Pride and Prejudice for teenagers.

If you think old novels are boring, try Pride and Prejudice by Jane Austen. Elizabeth Bennet is clever, funny and quick to judge, especially when it comes to the proud Mr. Darcy. As the story unfolds, both of them learn how wrong first impressions can be. The book is full of sharp conversations, silly relatives and a love story that still feels fresh.
My dad is turning 50. Help me write a speech, about 120 words, for his birthday dinner. I'm his daughter, and I'm 22.

Good evening, everyone. Thank you for coming to celebrate Papa's fiftieth birthday. Papa, you have always said that you don't like speeches, so I'll keep this short. When I was little, you taught me to ride a scooter, solve sums in my head and never leave a plate half-eaten. When I was a teenager, you waited up every night I came home late, pretending to read the newspaper. And when I moved away for college, you called every evening just to ask if I had eaten. You are the calmest, kindest and funniest man I know. Here's to fifty years of you, and many, many more. Happy birthday, Papa. We love you.
My grandfather has just come home after a knee operation. Write a welcome-home note from the grandchildren, under 50 words.

Welcome home, Dadu! We missed you so much. Your chair has been waiting for you, and so has your chess board. Rest well, take it slowly and let us fetch things for you. We promise to be quiet, mostly.
Love,
Aarohi, Kiaan and Myra
Draft a short announcement, around 60 words, for a free weekend reading class for the children of construction workers near our society.

Free Reading Class for Children
Starting this Saturday, volunteers from Sunrise Society will run a free reading class for the children of workers at the nearby construction site. Classes will be held every Saturday and Sunday from 4 to 5 pm in the society garden. Children aged 5 to 12 are welcome. Books, notebooks and snacks will be provided. More volunteers are always welcome.
Describe a street musician playing the flute at a railway station, in about 80 words.

On platform three, among the rushing passengers and the rattle of trolleys, an old man sits cross-legged on a folded blanket and plays the flute. His tune is slow and gentle, rising above the announcements and the hiss of the trains. Most people hurry past without looking. But a little girl stops, holding her mother's hand, and sways in time. A porter sets down his load to listen. For a few minutes, the busy station feels soft and still.
Write a short fable, about 90 words, about a hare and a tortoise, but this time the tortoise is the proud one.

After winning the famous race, the tortoise became very proud. He told every animal in the forest that he was the fastest creature alive. One day, he challenged the hare again. This time, the hare did not stop to sleep. He ran straight to the finish line and waited under a tree. The tortoise arrived hours later, puffing and embarrassed. The hare simply smiled and offered him some water. "We each win some races," he said kindly. The tortoise never boasted again. Moral: one win does not make you the best.
Write an email, under 60 words, asking my colleague Joseph to swap shifts with me next Friday.

Subject: Shift swap request for next Friday
Hi Joseph,
Could we swap shifts next Friday? I'm on the morning shift, but I have a family event that day. I could take your evening shift, and you could have my morning slot instead. Please tell me if that works for you.
Thanks,
Nirmala
A five-sentence description of a sunflower field for my photography caption, please.

The sunflower field stretched all the way to the hills. Thousands of golden heads turned together to face the morning sun. Bees moved lazily from flower to flower, heavy with pollen. A narrow dirt path ran through the middle, just wide enough for one person. Standing there, I felt as if I was walking through a field of small suns.
Write a message to my friends from abroad, about 70 words, explaining what Raksha Bandhan is.

Hi everyone! Today is Raksha Bandhan, a festival that celebrates the bond between brothers and sisters. Sisters tie a colourful thread called a rakhi on their brothers' wrists and pray for their well-being. In return, brothers give gifts and promise to always look out for their sisters. Many people also tie rakhis for cousins and close friends. The day is full of sweets, family visits and plenty of teasing.
I bought a pressure cooker that stopped working after a week. Write a polite complaint letter to the shop, about 90 words.

Dear Sir or Madam,
I purchased a 5-litre pressure cooker from your shop on 2 October, bill number 2387. Unfortunately, after only a week of use, the whistle stopped working, and the lid no longer seals properly. I have used it carefully and followed the instructions. As the product is still under warranty, I request a replacement or a repair at the earliest. I have attached a copy of the bill. Please tell me when I can bring the cooker to your shop.
Yours faithfully,
Revathi Nair
We're making a farewell card for our Class 12 seniors. Write a 50-word message from the juniors.

Dear Seniors,
Thank you for showing us the ropes, cheering for us at every event and lending us your old notes. The corridors won't be the same without you. We wish you the very best for your exams and the exciting years ahead. Come back and visit us!
With love,
Class 11
My grandparents just got their first smartphone. Write a short welcome message, about 50 words, for the family group.

Welcome to the family group, Nana and Nani! We're so happy you're here. Now you can see photos of the children every day and send us voice messages whenever you like. Don't worry if you press the wrong button. Everyone does at first. We're all here to help!
I'm 22 and moving to a new city alone for my first job. Write a short diary entry, about 90 words, about my first night there.

Dear Diary,
First night in Hyderabad. My rented room smells of fresh paint and has one chair, one bed and a fan that clicks every few seconds. I ate dinner from a takeaway box while sitting on the floor. It felt strange to have no one call me for dinner or ask about my day. I almost cried while unpacking Ma's pickle jar. But then I opened the window and heard children playing downstairs. This city doesn't know me yet. Tomorrow, I start my first job.
Write a funny note, under 40 words, to stick on the office fridge about someone eating other people's lunch.

Dear Lunch Thief,
We know you're hungry. We also know my paneer sandwich did not walk away by itself. Please bring your own lunch, or leave a thank-you note. Our tiffins have feelings too.
- A Very Hungry Colleague
Describe the atmosphere at a local football match on a muddy field, around 100 words.

The rain had stopped an hour before kick-off, but the field was still a sea of mud. That did not keep anyone away. Fans lined the edges, standing on bricks and benches to get a better view. Children perched on the wall with packets of peanuts. Every time a player slid and fell, the crowd roared with laughter. By half-time, nobody could tell the two teams apart, because both sets of jerseys were brown. When the only goal came in the eightieth minute, the whole crowd ran onto the field, slipping and hugging in the mud.
Explain to my 8-year-old, in about 60 words, why we visit art galleries.

An art gallery is a bit like a library, but instead of reading stories, we look at them. Each painting or sculpture is an artist's way of sharing an idea, a feeling or a memory. When we visit, we can ask ourselves, "What do I see? How does it make me feel?" There are no wrong answers. It's a fun way to learn to look closely.
Write a short note to myself, under 50 words, to read before exams when I feel stressed.

Take a deep breath. You have prepared for this, even if it doesn't feel like enough. One question at a time, one page at a time. Your marks do not decide your worth. Whatever happens, you will be okay, and the people who love you will still love you.
